A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QpiGNN study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–N support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 19 synthetic and real-world graph datasets, including baseline comparisons, perturbation tests, structural transfer, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark, robustness, transfer, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendix A retain the same GNN encoder, dual prediction and softplus-width heads, symmetric intervals, and joint coverage, violation, and width objective. The training algorithm is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine synthetic and ten real-world datasets and retain the same noise, edge-dropout, structured-split, and cross-graph transfer scenarios. The added main-text plots use previously represented data.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes the evidential-regression baseline ER-GNN from both dataset blocks, although the baseline description still names it. Other comparators remain; SQR and RQRadj. are shortened labels for the earlier GNN baselines.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings remain unchanged, including 90% target coverage, two-layer GraphSAGE with hidden size 64, 500 training epochs, and the optimizer settings. No revised evaluation protocol is established by the redisplayed figures.

E4.justification: The loss and architecture ablations, sensitivity analyses, perturbation tests, and structural-transfer analyses are retained. The convergence panel added to Figure 2 and the cases plotted in new Figure 3 already appear in v1 Appendices C.3 and K.

E5.justification: v2 removes every ± uncertainty value from the primary 19-dataset Table 1. For example, CF-GNN's BA MPIW changes from 68.27 ± 76.41 to 68.27. These summaries are not relocated to the appendices. Reported run counts and existing graphical error bars remain unchanged, so this is a substantial reporting loss rather than evidence of fewer runs.

E6.justification: ER-GNN's PICP/MPIW entries across all 19 datasets disappear from Table 1, including its ER-graph results of 0.72/1.86. All retained Table 1 means and matched appendix numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same coverage, width-optimality, and convergence statements, assumptions, and proofs. The added limitations discussion does not revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same quantile-free framework, dual-head architecture, theoretical guarantees, and robustness claims, including the headline 22% higher coverage and 50% narrower intervals across 19 benchmarks.

C2.justification: The new paragraph after Section 4.3.4 largely repeats existing independence and symmetry caveats, but additionally identifies backbone sensitivity, adaptive width-penalty tuning through annealing or meta-learning, and asymmetric interval construction as unresolved directions.

D1.justification: The introduction and Appendix G replace anonymous code and generation-script links with the named sybeam27/QpiGNN GitHub repository. Figure 3's new caption explicitly documents a width penalty of 0.5 and 500 epochs. Other implementation and hardware descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain unchanged. Angelopoulos and Bates is updated from its 2021 preprint to the 2023 publication of the same work; other bibliography edits concern capitalization and publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief background explanations, revises the qualitative-evaluation paragraph, numbers the experimental-setting subsections, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. The overall narrative and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reformatted and enlarged, Figure 2 gains the existing real-world convergence panel, and Figure 3 redisplays selected interval plots. Figure 3(b) is incorrectly captioned Anaheim: its curves match the PTBR/Twitch panel in v1 Figure 9 and retained v2 Figure 10. Subsequent figures are renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves visibility of existing illustrations and adds useful documentation and qualifications. However, removing Table 1's uncertainty summaries and ER-GNN results reduces empirical transparency, while Figure 3(b) introduces a dataset-labeling error. These losses outweigh the limited presentation gains; the underlying method, theory, and retained numerical findings remain unchanged.
